newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P rates Nat Bank NZ senior Euro notes AA-/A-1+.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Nat Bank NZ senior Euro notes AA-/A-1+.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard and Poor's on Friday said it had assigned its AA-/A-1+ ratings to the senior notes issued under National Bank of New Zealand's US$500 million Euro medium term note programme.
S&P also assigned its A+ rating to the dated subordinated debt and an A rating to the undated subordinated debt, reflecting the junior status of these obligations.
"The outlook on the long-term ratings is stable," S&P said.

It said the ratings were based on the National Bank of New Zealand's (NBNZ) ownership by, and integration with, its parent bank, Britain's Lloyds TSB Group Plc. Lloyds TSB is the second largest financial services group in the United Kingdom based on market capitalisation.
"In addition, the rating reflects NBNZ's own sound market position and business profile," S&P said.
"During fiscal 1996, NBNZ recorded 17.3 percent growth in loan assets, primarily as a result of strong underlying growth in the residential housing portfolio.
"The loan book is well diversified, although like many banks operating in the market, NBNZ maintains a relatively high exposure to the rural sector."

S&P said although NBNZ's profitability deteriorated in fiscal 1996, and the competitive pressures in the New Zealand market showed no signs of abating, the outlook was supported by NBNZ's strong market position and the bank's continuing focus on cost controls and improved efficiencies.
